chunks.title: MTF Configuration File – Overview
chunks.content:
The MTF (Modular Test Framework) configuration file is a YAML-format file that is essential for the MTF framework. MTF requires assigning logical channels to physical channels to specify which hardware interface should be used for data reception and transmission. The configuration file defines this assignment.

One key benefit: the same test cases can run on different hardware setups. To adapt to a new setup, users only need to update the physical channel information, keeping the logical channels and test cases unchanged. This supports the framework's main goal of abstraction — instead of specifying the exact physical channel, test cases refer to a logical channel name, and the MTF handles the rest.
chunks.summary: YAML-based MTF Configuration File maps logical channels to physical hardware, enabling test reuse across different setups.

chunks.title: MTF Configuration File – File Structure
chunks.content:
The MTF Configuration File is composed of three main sections (plus one optional):

1. **Channels** (mandatory): Defines logical channels — the virtual representations of physical communication buses and interfaces (CAN, LIN, Ethernet, FlexRay, I/O, Serial, etc.).

2. **Mappings** (mandatory): Maps each logical channel to a physical device. The order of sections does not affect interpretation, but the order shown here is preferred for clarity.

3. **FrameworkConfig** (optional): Defines tracer configuration, internal module settings, connected ECUs, service packs, Ethernet configuration, and diagnostics.

4. **ChannelsConfig** (optional): Provides additional per-channel configuration such as FaultyChannels for fault injection testing.

Note: All field names are case-sensitive.
chunks.summary: The MTF config file has Channels and Mappings (mandatory), plus FrameworkConfig and ChannelsConfig (optional). All field names are case-sensitive.

chunks.title: Section 1: Channels – Overview
chunks.content:
The first step in creating the MTF configuration file is to define the Channels section. This section describes logical channels, which will later be linked to real (physical) channels in the Mappings section.

A logical channel is an abstraction — a virtual representation of a real hardware channel. Physical channels can be of different types: bus interfaces (CAN, LIN, FlexRay, Ethernet), I/O lines, or serial ports.

Before defining channels, you should be familiar with the available hardware in your test bench. You don't need to include all hardware channels — only the ones required for the current test case. Use clear and meaningful names, e.g., 'can_ch1' or 'eth_switch'.
chunks.summary: The Channels section defines logical channels as virtual representations of physical buses and interfaces.

chunks.title: Section 1: Channels – YAML Section Structure
chunks.content:
The Channels section uses the key `Channels:` at the root level. Under it, each logical channel is defined by a custom name (the YAML key). Under each channel name, properties are listed as key-value pairs.

YAML uses indentation to show hierarchy — use spaces (not tabs).

Example:
```yaml
Channels:
 CAN_channel:
  Id: 1                        # Required
  Type: CAN                    # Required
  Protocol: CAN2.0             # Optional
  loggingName: CAN_channel     # Optional
  Alias: [Ch_CAN, Chan_CAN]    # Optional
  TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_CAN # Optional
 CAN_FD_channel:
  Id: 2
  Type: CAN
  Protocol: CANFD
  Alias: [Ch_CAN_FD]
  TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_CAN
 ETH_SOMEIP:
  Id: 3
  Type: ETHERNET
  TracerName: PCAP_Tracer_SOMEIP
```

The order of properties within a channel does not affect interpretation.
chunks.summary: Channels are declared under Channels: key. Each named channel entry has Id, Type, and optional Protocol, Alias, TracerName, loggingName.

chunks.title: Section 1: Channels – Field Descriptions (Id, Type, Protocol, Alias, TracerName …)
chunks.content:
Detailed description of all fields in a logical channel definition:

**ChannelName** (mandatory): The YAML key — the logical channel name. Must be unique and meaningful. Use numbers (not at the start) and underscores; no spaces. Examples: Eth_ch, CAN_ch, CAN2_ch.

**Id** (mandatory): A unique user-defined integer ID for the logical channel. Each channel in the file must have a different Id value.

**Type** (mandatory): Specifies the protocol used for communication. Available values:
- CAN, CAN-FD → for CAN channels
- LIN → for LIN channels
- FR, FLEXRAY → for FlexRay channels
- ETHERNET → for Ethernet channels
- IOOUTPUT, IOINPUT → for I/O channels
- IOSERIAL, SERIAL → for serial channels
- PS → for power supply channels
- BRIDGE → for bridge/TUN-TAP channels

**Protocol** (conditional): Mandatory when complex hardware architecture requires specifying the protocol version. Examples by Type:
- CAN: CAN2.0, CAN-IB500, CANFD, CANFD-IDENTICAL-ArbPh-DataPh
- LIN: LIN1.2, LIN2.3

**Alias** (optional): One or multiple alternative names for the channel used in test cases. Same naming rules as ChannelName. Example: Alias: [Ch_CAN, Chan_CAN].

**loggingName** (optional): A specific logging name used during ASCII or PCAPNG tracing.

**TracerName** (optional): Name of the tracer linked to this channel (defined in FrameworkConfig). Used for logging traffic of this specific channel.

**LoggingBusIndex** (optional): Specific to IO ASCII Tracing. Configures the logging index for the channel.
chunks.summary: Logical channel fields: ChannelName (mandatory key), Id (mandatory unique integer), Type (mandatory protocol: CAN/LIN/ETHERNET/FR/IOOUTPUT/IOINPUT/SERIAL/PS/BRIDGE), Protocol (conditional), Alias (optional), loggingName (optional), TracerName (optional).

chunks.title: Section 1: Channels – Complete Setup Example
chunks.content:
Step-by-step example creating a Channels section for a setup with: 1 Ethernet switch, 2 CAN buses (4 channels: CAN-FD for bus1, CAN for bus2), 1 FlexRay bus (2 channels).

```yaml
Channels:
 Ethernet_Switch:
   Id: 8
   Type: ETHERNET
   TracerName: ETH_PCAP_Tracer
 CAN_FD1_ch1:
   Id: 9
   TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_CAN
   Type: CANFD
   Protocol: CANFD
 CAN_FD2_ch1:
   Id: 10
   TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_CAN
   Type: CANFD
   Protocol: CANFD
 CAN1_ch2:
   Id: 11
   TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_CAN
   Type: CAN
   Protocol: CAN2.0
 CAN2_ch2:
   Id: 12
   TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_CAN
   Type: CAN
   Protocol: CAN2.0
 FlexRay_ch1:
   Id: 13
   TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_FLEXRAY
   LoggingName: A_FlexRay
   Type: FR
 FlexRay_ch2:
   Id: 14
   TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_FLEXRAY
   LoggingName: Ab_FlexRay
   Type: FR
```
chunks.summary: Complete Channels section example with Ethernet, two CAN buses (CAN-FD + CAN2.0), and FlexRay channels.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mappings – Overview
chunks.content:
After defining logical channels in the Channels section, the next step is to map each one to a physical channel/device in the Mappings section. This tells MTF which hardware resource to use when a logical channel is referenced in a test case.

Supported device types in Mappings:
- **CM** (Capture Module): Technica device for CAN, LIN, FlexRay capture
- **BTS-Revo**: Body Electronics Test System for I/O simulation and fault injection
- **PCAP**: Network adapters for Ethernet traffic
- **Genesys_PowerSupply** / **Manson_PowerSupply**: Power supply devices
- **Serial**: Serial port communication
- **HH_Electrical_load**: H&H electrical load devices
- **Lf_Reader**: LF antenna reader (BTS-Revo extension)
- **RelayBoards**: Technica relay boards (SHS)
- **HIDRelayBoards**: DCTTECH relay boards
- **WinpkFilter**: Windows packet filter
- **TUNTAP_BRIDGE**: TUN/TAP bridge channels
- **EES**: Time synchronization source
- **TE-Analog**: Analog channels
- **Shelly relay**: Ethernet-controlled relay
chunks.summary: The Mappings section links logical channels to physical devices: CM, BTS-Revo, PCAP adapters, power supplies, serial ports, relay boards, etc.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mappings – YAML Section Structure
chunks.content:
The Mappings section starts with `Mappings:`. Each top-level entry represents a hardware category or device type, indented with two spaces.

```yaml
Mappings:
  CM:
    Devices:
      1:
        Id: 64
        Type: CAN_Combo
        Buses:
          CAN_channel:
            HWChannel: 619
            OperationMode: Normal
  BTS-Revo:
    Boards:
      1:
        Id: 160
        IOs:
          Ch1-BTS:
            HWChannel: 1
            MeasurementAttribute: Voltage
  PCAP:
    1:
      Adapter:
        Name: ETH_channel
        FriendlyName: "Ethernet"
  Genesys_PowerSupply:
    Channels:
      1:
        ChannelName: PS_Channel
  Manson_PowerSupply:
    Channels:
      1:
        ChannelName: PS_Channel
  Serial:
    Ports:
      Master-Serial:
        PortName: COM3
        BaudRate: 9600
  VirtualDevices:
    Buses:
      CAN_channel:
        Name: CAN_channel
```
chunks.summary: Mappings section structure: top-level device types (CM, BTS-Revo, PCAP, Power Supply, Serial, VirtualDevices) each containing device-specific sub-sections.

chunks.subsection: Mapping to Capture Module – Common Fields
chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping to Capture Module – Fields (Id, Type, Buses, HWChannel, OperationMode)
chunks.content:
The Capture Module (CM) is a Technica device that records vehicle communication (CAN, LIN, FlexRay, Ethernet).

Under `CM: → Devices: → 1:` (or 2:, 3: for multiple devices), the fields are:

**Id** (mandatory): Last byte of the CM IP address. Example: CM IP 10.104.3.64 → Id: 64.

**Type** (mandatory): CM type. Valid values: `CAN_Combo`, `LIN_Combo`.

**Buses** (mandatory): Dictionary of logical channel names mapped to this CM. Under each channel name:
  - **HWChannel** (mandatory): Channel ID from the CM web interface.
  - **OperationMode** (optional): Normal (Rx+Tx), Spy (listen only, no ACK), TxOnly, RxOnly.

Example:
```yaml
Mappings:
  CM:
    Devices:
      1:
        Id: 64
        Type: CAN_Combo
        Buses:
          CAN_channel1:
            HWChannel: 619
            OperationMode: Normal
      2:
        Id: 48
        Type: LIN_Combo
        Buses:
          LIN_channel1:
            HWChannel: 536
            OperationMode: Normal
```
chunks.summary: CM mapping: Id = last IP byte, Type = CAN_Combo or LIN_Combo, Buses = dict of channel→HWChannel + OperationMode (Normal/Spy/TxOnly/RxOnly).

chunks.subsection: Mapping to Capture Module – FlexRay Fields
chunks.title: Section 2: CM Mapping – FlexRay-Specific Fields (KeySlot, NodeType, WakeUpCluster)
chunks.content:
FlexRay channels mapped to a Capture Module require three additional fields:

**KeySlot**: A static slot used by the CM to transmit sync and startup frames. Required when NodeType is ColdStartLeading or ColdStartFollowing.

**NodeType** (mandatory for FlexRay): FlexRay node type. Values:
- ColdStartLeading
- ColdStartFollowing
- NonColdStartNonSync
- NonColdStartSync

**WakeUpCluster**: Boolean. Whether to transmit a wake-up pattern on the cluster.

Example:
```yaml
Mappings:
  CM:
    Devices:
      1:
        Id: 65
        Type: CAN_Combo
        Busses:
          A_FlexRay:
            OperationMode: Normal
            HWChannel: 358
            KeySlot: 1
            NodeType: ColdStartFollowing
            WakeUpCluster: false
```
chunks.summary: FlexRay CM mapping adds KeySlot, NodeType (ColdStartLeading/Following/NonColdStart*), and WakeUpCluster fields.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping to Power Supply (Genesys, Manson) – Fields
chunks.content:
MTF supports Genesys and Manson power supplies. Common fields under `Genesys_PowerSupply: → Channels: → 1:`:

**ChannelName** (mandatory): Logical channel name from the Channels section.
**DefaultVoltage** (optional): Default output voltage.
**MaxVoltage** (mandatory): Maximum allowed voltage.
**DefaultMaxCurrent** (mandatory): Default current limit.
**SamplingInterval** (optional): Interval between power measurements in ms (default 100 ms).
**ContinuousMonitoringActive** (optional): Continuously read voltage/current.
**KeepStatus** (optional): Keep PS ON between test cases.

**Genesys-specific** (TCP/Serial communication):
- **CommunicationProtocol**: Serial or Tcp
- For Serial: **PortName** (e.g., COM2), **BitRate** (e.g., 19200)
- For Tcp: **IP**, **Port**, **Language** (SCPI or GEN)

**Manson-specific** (serial):
- **PortName** (mandatory), **BitRate** (mandatory)
- **MaxVoltage**, **MaxCurrent** (mandatory), **DefaultVoltage** (optional)

Example (Genesys via TCP):
```yaml
Genesys_PowerSupply:
  Channels:
    1:
      ChannelName: PS_Channel
      DefaultMaxCurrent: 35
      DefaultVoltage: 12
      MaxVoltage: 20
      CommunicationProtocol: Tcp
      Language: SCPI
      IP: 169.254.16.136
      Port: 8003
```
chunks.summary: Power supply mapping (Genesys/Manson): ChannelName, MaxVoltage, DefaultMaxCurrent mandatory; communication via TCP (IP/Port/Language) or Serial (PortName/BitRate).

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping to Network Adapter (PCAP) – Fields
chunks.content:
Network adapters (Ethernet interfaces) are mapped under `PCAP: → 1: → Adapter:`.

Key fields:
**Name** (mandatory): The logical channel name from the Channels section.
**FriendlyName** (or AdapterFriendlyName): Windows adapter friendly name (Control Panel → Network Connections).
**Interface**: Adapter system name if FriendlyName not used. Windows: 'DeviceNPF_{GUID}'; Linux: 'enp0s4'.
**BufferSize**: Kernel buffer size in MB.
**BpfFilter**: Packet filter (e.g., 'ip src 192.168.0.1').
**Timeout**: Read timeout in ms.
**TimeStampPrecision**: Microsecond or Nanosecond (Linux only for Nanosecond).
**TimeStampSource**: TimeStampHost, TimeStampHostLowPrecision, TimeStampAdapter, etc.
**ImmediateMode**: true = deliver packets immediately without buffering.
**SnapshotLength**: Capture snapshot length.
**PcapDeviceMode**: Promiscuous mode captures all packets.
**PacketProcessingActive**: false = adapter used for logging only.
**PacketIdentificationActive**: false = forward all traffic without SOME/IP/DOIP identification.
**UseDataLoggerTimeStamp**: Replace software timestamp with hardware logger timestamp.
**DataLoggerType**: TECMP, CMP, or NotDefined.

Example:
```yaml
PCAP:
  1:
    Adapter:
      Name: ETH_SOMEIP
      FriendlyName: "Ethernet-ch"
      BufferSize: 8
      Timeout: 1
      ImmediateMode: true
      SnapshotLength: 65536
      PcapDeviceMode: promiscuous
      PacketProcessingActive: true
      PacketIdentificationActive: true
```
chunks.summary: PCAP network adapter mapping: Name (logical channel), FriendlyName (Windows adapter), BufferSize, Timeout, ImmediateMode, PcapDeviceMode, PacketProcessingActive.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping to BTS-Revo – Fields (Id, IOs, HWChannel, MeasurementAttribute)
chunks.content:
The BTS-REVO (Body Electronics Test System) simulates buttons, sensors, actuators, and fault conditions (short to GND, short to VBAT, open load).

Structure: `BTS-Revo: → Boards: → 1:` (for each board).

**Id** (mandatory): Last byte of the BTS-Revo IP address. The full IP is on the device back; set the last byte with the rotary switch. E.g., position 0 → Id = 160.

**IOs** (mandatory): Dictionary of logical channel names.
Under each channel name:
  - **HWChannel** (mandatory): Physical pin index (1–24, left to right).
  - **MeasurementAttribute** (mandatory): Voltage, Current, or PWM.
  - **Function** (mandatory): None, Relay, Potentiometer, ElectronicLoad, GNDSwitch, VBATSwitch, VoltageGenerator, etc.
  - **LineContactState** (optional): Open Load state active by default.
  - **GndContactState** (optional): Short to GND active by default.
  - **VbatContactState** (optional): VBAT state active by default.
  - **InitValue** (optional): Default resistance, voltage, or other value.
  - **StaticChannel** (optional): State cannot be changed by test cases.

Example:
```yaml
BTS-Revo:
  Boards:
    1:
      Id: 160
      IOs:
        Ch1-BTS:
          HWChannel: 1
          MeasurementAttribute: Voltage
        Ch3-BTS:
          HWChannel: 3
          Function: VBATSwitch
          MeasurementAttribute: Voltage
```
chunks.summary: BTS-Revo mapping: Id = last IP byte, IOs = dict of channel→HWChannel (1-24) + MeasurementAttribute (Voltage/Current/PWM) + Function.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping to Serial Port – Fields (PortName, BaudRate, Parity, StopBits …)
chunks.content:
Serial channels are mapped under `Serial: → Ports: → <LogicalChannelName>:`.

**PortName** (mandatory): OS serial port identifier (e.g., COM13, /dev/ttyUSB0).
**BaudRate** (mandatory): Communication baud rate (e.g., 9600, 115200).
**Parity** (optional): None, Even, Odd.
**DataBits** (optional): Character size (e.g., 8).
**StopBits** (optional): Number of stop bits (e.g., One).
**FlowControl** (optional): None, Hardware, Software.
**MessageTerminator** (optional): End-of-line character (e.g., '\r\n', '\r').
**MaxReceivedDataSize** (optional): Maximum message size in bytes.
**SeparationTimeMs** (optional): Time between consecutive characters in ms.

Example:
```yaml
Serial:
  Ports:
    Master-Serial:
      PortName: COM13
      BaudRate: 9600
      Parity: None
      DataBits: 8
      StopBits: One
      FlowControl: None
      MessageTerminator: ""
      MaxReceivedDataSize: 512
```
chunks.summary: Serial port mapping: PortName and BaudRate mandatory; optional Parity, DataBits, StopBits, FlowControl, MessageTerminator.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping to HH Electrical Load – Fields
chunks.content:
H&H electrical loads (PLI / PMLI series) are mapped under `HH_Electrical_load: → Devices: → 1:`.

**Id** (mandatory): The device physical ID.
**PortName** (mandatory): COM port connected to the load.
**Type** (mandatory): PLI or PMLI (PMLI = multi-channel).
**BitRate** (mandatory): Serial baud rate (e.g., 115200).
**Channels**: Maps channel index to logical channel name.
  - **Id**: Channel index on the device.
  - **Name**: Logical channel name from the Channels section.
  - **ExternalTrigger** (optional): External I/O trigger (default false = remote).
  - **VoltageProtection** (optional): Voltage protection value.

Example:
```yaml
HH_Electrical_load:
  Devices:
    1:
      Id: 2
      PortName: COM19
      Type: PLI
      BitRate: 115200
      Channels:
        1:
          Id: 1
          Name: HH
```
chunks.summary: HH Electrical Load mapping: Id, PortName, Type (PLI/PMLI), BitRate mandatory; Channels maps index to logical channel name.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping to LF Reader (BTS-Revo Extension)
chunks.content:
LF_Reader is an extension board for BTS-Revo with a maximum of 3 antennas per board.

Structure: `Lf_Reader: → 1:` (board index).

**BoardId** (mandatory): The board with LF_reader extension ID.
**Antennas**: Dictionary of antenna definitions:
  - **AntennaNumber**: The antenna number.
  - **HWChannel**: The channel of the LF_Reader.

Example:
```yaml
Lf_Reader:
  1:
    BoardId: 169
    Antennas:
      1:
        AntennaNumber: 1
        HWChannel: 1
      2:
        AntennaNumber: 2
        HWChannel: 2
```
chunks.summary: LF_Reader (BTS-Revo extension): BoardId mandatory, Antennas dict maps AntennaNumber to HWChannel (max 3 antennas).

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping to Relay Boards (Technica SHS) – Fields
chunks.content:
Technica Relay Boards (SHS) are mapped under `RelayBoards:`.

**CANChannelName** (mandatory): Name of the CAN channel connected to the relay boards CAN bus.
**Boards**: List of connected relay boards.
  - **Id** (mandatory): Board ID.
  - **Relays**: List of relay channels.
    - **RELAY_NAME**:
      - **HWChannel** (mandatory): Channel ID on the relay (starting from 1).
      - **Function**: Must be `Relay`.
      - **InitValue** (optional): ON or OFF (default OFF).
      - **DefaultValue** (optional): ON or OFF (default OFF).

Example:
```yaml
RelayBoards:
  CANChannelName: RELAY_BOARDS_CAN
  Boards:
    1:
      Id: 1
      Relays:
        RELAY_A:
          HWChannel: 1
          Function: Relay
    2:
      Id: 2
      Relays:
        RELAY_B:
          HWChannel: 1
          InitValue: ON
          DefaultValue: ON
          Function: Relay
```
chunks.summary: Technica SHS relay boards: CANChannelName + Boards list each with Id and Relays (HWChannel, Function=Relay, InitValue, DefaultValue).

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping to HIDRelayBoards (DCTTECH) – Fields
chunks.content:
DCTTECH HID relay boards are mapped under `HIDRelayBoards:` as a map of global IDs to board definitions.

**ID** (mandatory): Board serial number (obtainable via TestApp 'Find device' button).
**Relays**: List of relay channels (define channels as IOOUTPUT type in Channels section).
  - **HWChannel** (mandatory): Channel ID on the relay.
  - **InitValue** (optional): ON or OFF.
  - **DefaultValue** (optional): ON or OFF.

Example:
```yaml
HIDRelayBoards:
  1:
    ID: Board1SerialId
    Relays:
      RELAY_C:
        HWChannel: 1
        InitValue: ON
        DefaultValue: OFF
  2:
    ID: Board2SerialId
    Relays:
      RELAY_E:
        HWChannel: 8
```
chunks.summary: DCTTECH HID relay boards: global ID (board serial), Relays map with HWChannel, InitValue, DefaultValue.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping WinpkFilter Channels – Fields
chunks.content:
WinpkFilter enables packet filtering on Windows Ethernet adapters. Requires the Windows Packet Filter driver (wiresock/ndisapi).

Structure: `WinpkFilter: → CHANNEL_NAME:`.

**AdpaterFriendlyName** (mandatory): Name of the corresponding Ethernet adapter.
**Type**: Filter or FilterFastIO.
**IPMacTable**: List of [IP, MAC] pairs.
**VLans**: VLAN configuration with InnerTags and/or OuterTags.
  - Each tag: ID (Vlan ID), Priority, IPList.
**IPV4Ttl**: TTL value for outgoing IPv4 packets.

Example:
```yaml
WinpkFilter:
  ETH_Sender:
    AdpaterFriendlyName: ETH_Sender
    Type: Filter
    IPMacTable:
      [[160.48.249.13, 00:50:c2:e4:30:0d]]
    VLans:
      InnerTags:
        - ID: 68
          Priority: 7
          IPList: [160.48.249.13]
```
chunks.summary: WinpkFilter maps Ethernet channels with AdpaterFriendlyName, Type (Filter/FilterFastIO), IPMacTable, and VLAN InnerTags/OuterTags.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping TUN/TAP Bridge Channels – Fields
chunks.content:
TUN/TAP enables bridging multiple virtual adapters with a physical adapter, with VLAN tagging/stripping at the bridge level.

First, define an ETHERNET channel with type BRIDGE in Channels section:
```yaml
Channels:
  ETH_Bridge:
    Id: 90
    Type: BRIDGE
```

Then in Mappings under `TUNTAP_BRIDGE: → ETH_Bridge:`:
**Name**: Ethernet bridge channel name.
**PhysicalAdapter**: Friendly name of the physical adapter.
**TunTapAdapterList → TunTapAdapter**:
  - **Name**: Virtual adapter friendly name.
  - **InnerVlan** / **OuterVlan**: VLAN config (VlanId, VlanEthertype, VlanPriorityTag, VlanCfi).
  - **ManipulatePackets** (optional): Enable dynamic VLAN tagging from EthernetTopology.
chunks.summary: TUN/TAP bridge: define BRIDGE-type channel, then TUNTAP_BRIDGE mapping with PhysicalAdapter and virtual TunTapAdapters with VLAN configs.

chunks.title: Section 2: EES Time Synchronization – GrandMaster Field
chunks.content:
The TE EES (Ethernet Edge Switch) provides nanosecond-level time synchronization to PTP clients (CM, BTSEvo boards). This section specifies which EES acts as the GrandMaster.

**GrandMaster** (mandatory): ID of the EES responsible for time synchronization.

Example:
```yaml
EES:
  GrandMaster: 200
```
chunks.summary: EES section: GrandMaster field sets the ID of the EES that acts as the PTP time synchronization source.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping TE-Analog Channels – Fields (HWChannel, DeviceId)
chunks.content:
TE-Analog covers all analog channels from different devices (LIN/CM-sense, etc.).

Structure: `TE-Analog: → ChannelName:`

Under each channel name:
**HWChannel** (mandatory): Physical channel ID on the device (can be hex, e.g., 0x500).
**DeviceId** (mandatory): ID of the device the channel is connected to.

Example:
```yaml
TE-Analog:
  Analog_48_C:
    HWChannel: 0x500
    DeviceId: 48
  Analog_48_A:
    HWChannel: 0x501
    DeviceId: 48
```
chunks.summary: TE-Analog mapping: each channel name maps to HWChannel (physical channel ID, can be hex) and DeviceId.

chunks.title: Section 2: Mapping Shelly Relay – Fields
chunks.content:
Shelly relays are Ethernet-controlled relays mapped under `Devices:`.

**CommunicationProtocol** (mandatory): HTTP or MQTT (currently only HTTP supported).
**IP** (mandatory): Device IP address.
**Port** (mandatory): Communication port.
**Channels**: Dict of logical channel names.
  - **ID** (mandatory): Channel ID on the Shelly device.
  - **DoRestart** (optional): Boolean, reset at MTF startup.
  - **RestartDuration** (optional): Duration of restart in ms (default 3000 ms).
  - **DurationAfterRestart** (optional): Wait time after restart in ms (default 3000 ms).

Example:
```yaml
Devices:
  1:
    CommunicationProtocol: HTTP
    IP: 192.168.0.201
    Port: 80
    Channels:
      TEST_IO_5:
        ID: 1
        DoRestart: True
        RestartDuration: 3000
```
chunks.summary: Shelly relay mapping: HTTP/MQTT protocol, IP, Port, and Channels with ID, DoRestart, RestartDuration.

chunks.title: Section 3: FrameworkConfig – Overview
chunks.content:
The FrameworkConfig section configures various aspects of the framework:

- **Tracing**: Configure PCAP and ASCII tracers for logging traffic.
- **ConnectedEcus**: List the ECUs/DUTs connected to the test bench.
- **ServicePack**: Specify an OEM service pack instead of individual ECUs.
- **PublisherConfig**: Configure the Publish/Subscribe event dispatching model.
- **EthernetConfig**: Ethernet-specific settings (NPdu, SomeIP, VLAN, AppLayer ports).
- **EthernetTopology**: Define Ethernet ECUs and their MAC/IP/VLAN data.
- **ChannelToEcusMapping**: Link ECUs to their Ethernet transmission adapters.
- **Diagnostics**: DoIP/HSFZ diagnostics protocol configuration.

Example structure:
```yaml
FrameworkConfig:
  Tracing:
    PCAP_Tracer_1: ...
    ASCII_Tracer_1: ...
  ConnectedEcus:
    - ECU1
    - ECU2
  PublisherConfig:
    PublisherType: MultiThreaded
```
chunks.summary: FrameworkConfig section configures tracers, connected ECUs, publisher model, Ethernet settings, and diagnostics.

chunks.title: FrameworkConfig – PCAP Tracer Configuration
chunks.content:
PCAP tracers log Ethernet traffic. Defined under `FrameworkConfig: → Tracing: → TracerName:`.

Common fields:
**Type**: PCAP
**Timestamp**: Microsecond or Nanosecond
**LoggingType**: MultipleAdapterMode or PerformanceMode

**LoggerConfiguration → FileConfig**:
- **BaseFileName**: Base name for rotating log files (e.g., trace_eth_1).
- **Extension**: '.pcap', '.pcapng', or '.pcapng.zst' (Zstandard compression).
- **MaxFile**: Max number of rotating files.
- **MaxFileSize**: Max file size in MB before rotating.
- **CompressionLevel**: For .pcapng.zst only (MultipleAdapterMode only).

**LoggerConfiguration → BufferConfig**:
- **BufferSize**: Buffer size in MB.
- **BufferNumber**: (PerformanceMode only) Number of buffers.
- **WriteBurstSize**: (PerformanceMode only) Block write size.

Example (MultipleAdapterMode with compression):
```yaml
FrameworkConfig:
  Tracing:
    PCAP_Tracer_1:
      Type: PCAP
      LoggingType: MultipleAdapterMode
      Timestamp: Microsecond
      LoggerConfiguration:
        BufferConfig:
          BufferSize: 200
        FileConfig:
          BaseFileName: trace_1
          Extension: ".pcapng.zst"
          CompressionLevel: 5
```
chunks.summary: PCAP tracer: Type=PCAP, LoggingType (MultipleAdapterMode/PerformanceMode), FileConfig (BaseFileName, Extension, MaxFileSize) and BufferConfig.

chunks.title: FrameworkConfig – ASCII Tracer Configuration
chunks.content:
ASCII tracers log CAN/LIN/FlexRay traffic in text format. Defined under `FrameworkConfig: → Tracing: → TracerName:`.

**Type**: ASCII
**Base**: Hex or Decimal formatting.
**Timestamp**: Microsecond (ASCII supports only Microsecond).
**TimeStampSetting**: Absolute or Relative (to test case start).
**InternalEventLogged**: true/false — log internal events like LIN wake-up.

**LoggerConfiguration → FileConfig**:
- **BaseFileName**: Base name for rotating .asc files.
- **Extension**: e.g., '.asc'.
- **MaxFile**: Max number of rotating files.
- **MaxFileSize**: Max file size in MB.

Note: If testing ASCII Tracer locally (no hardware), add the channel to VirtualDevices.

Example:
```yaml
FrameworkConfig:
  Tracing:
    default_ascii_tracer:
      Type: ASCII
      Base: Hex
      InternalEventLogged: 'true'
      TimeStamp: Microsecond
      TimeStampSetting: Absolute
      LoggerConfiguration:
        FileConfig:
          BaseFileName: lin_can_trace
          Extension: .asc
          MaxFile: '150'
          MaxFileSize: '200'
```
chunks.summary: ASCII tracer: Type=ASCII, Base (Hex/Decimal), Timestamp=Microsecond, TimeStampSetting (Absolute/Relative), FileConfig for rotating .asc files.

chunks.title: FrameworkConfig – ConnectedEcus and ServicePack
chunks.content:
**ConnectedEcus**: List of ECU (Device Under Test) names connected to the test bench. Names must match ECU names defined in the database file (ARXML, DBC, LDF, FIBEX).

```yaml
FrameworkConfig:
  ConnectedEcus:
    - ECU1
    - ECU2
    - ECU3
```

**ServicePack**: Specifies an OEM service pack (group of ECUs) to start instead of listing individual ECUs under ConnectedEcus.

```yaml
FrameworkConfig:
  ServicePack: ServicePack_name
```
chunks.summary: ConnectedEcus lists DUT ECU names (matching database file); ServicePack specifies an OEM group of ECUs instead of individual listing.

chunks.title: FrameworkConfig – Publisher Configuration (PublisherType, ChannelsGroups)
chunks.content:
MTF implements a Publish/Subscribe model for event dispatching (e.g., received CAN frames).

**PublisherType** (mandatory): SingleThreaded or MultiThreaded.
- **SingleThreaded**: One thread for all event types.
- **MultiThreaded**: Multiple threads for event dispatching.

**ChannelsGroups** (only for MultiThreaded): Defines thread/channel mapping. Each group is a list of channel names that share a thread.

Example:
```yaml
FrameworkConfig:
  PublisherConfig:
    PublisherType: MultiThreaded
    ChannelsGroups:
      - [Ch_CAN1, Ch_CAN2, Ch_CAN3]
      - [ETH_SPY]
```
chunks.summary: PublisherConfig: PublisherType SingleThreaded or MultiThreaded; ChannelsGroups maps channel groups to threads (MultiThreaded only).

chunks.title: FrameworkConfig – Diagnostics Configuration (DoIP, HSFZ)
chunks.content:
Optional Diagnostics section configures protocol and addresses for diagnostic sessions.

**EcuIpAddress**: IP of the ECU to connect to. Use 'AutoDetect' for automatic detection.
**TestersIpAddress**: Tester address. Use 'Auto' for automatic assignment.
**Protocol**: HSFZ or DOIP.
**NetID** (optional): Net address of the target ECU. If not specified, identification requests are sent through all interfaces.

Example:
```yaml
FrameworkConfig:
  Diagnostics:
    EcuIpAddress: AutoDetect
    TestersIpAddress: 172.172.22.22
    Protocol: DOIP
    NetID: 160.48
```
chunks.summary: Diagnostics section: EcuIpAddress, TestersIpAddress, Protocol (DOIP/HSFZ), and optional NetID for targeted identification.

chunks.title: FrameworkConfig – Ethernet Configuration (NPduConfig, SomeIPConfig, AppLayerPorts)
chunks.content:
EthernetConfig under FrameworkConfig provides optional Ethernet-specific settings.

**ConsiderOnlyEthernetTopologyEcus** (optional, default false): Only consider ECUs from EthernetTopology section for COM Ethernet communication.

**NPduConfig** (optional):
- ManageVlansInCom: Add 802.1Q VLAN tags to NPDU packets.
- RestrictedNPduChannelsInCom: Only create COM NPDU packets for DuT ECU channels.
- IPMacTable: [[IP, MAC]] pairs.
- VLans: InnerTags and OuterTags (each with ID, Priority, IPList).

**SomeIPConfig** (optional):
- ServerToClientPortRangeMapping: Map server port ranges to client port ranges.
- EndpointImplementation: 'lwip' or 'boost' (default boost).

**AppLayerPorts** (optional): Ports for NPdu, SomeIp, UDPNM, DLT, SomeIpSD protocols.

Example:
```yaml
FrameworkConfig:
  EthernetConfig:
    ConsiderOnlyEthernetTopologyEcus: true
    AppLayerPorts:
      NPdu: [3000, [3100, 3200]]
      SomeIp: [[500, 503], 1000]
      UDPNM: [4100]
      DLT: [5000]
      SomeIpSD: [30490]
```
chunks.summary: EthernetConfig: NPduConfig (VLAN, IPMacTable), SomeIPConfig (port mapping), AppLayerPorts (NPdu/SomeIp/UDPNM/DLT/SomeIpSD), ConsiderOnlyEthernetTopologyEcus.

chunks.title: FrameworkConfig – EthernetTopology Configuration
chunks.content:
EthernetTopology defines Ethernet ECUs and their network data for packet manipulation.

**EthProtoPrioConfig**: List to set VLAN priority per Ethernet protocol.
- Protocol: TCP, UDP, ICMPv6
- DefaultPriority: 0–7
- Ports: Override priority for specific port/range (SrcPort, DstPort, Priority).

**TopologyConfig**: Per-ECU configuration.
- EcuName (optional): ECU identifier.
- SrcIpList (mandatory): List of ECU IP addresses.
- SrcMacAdr (optional): Source MAC address.
- TunTapAdapterName (optional): Links to a TunTap adapter.
- Vlans (optional): VLAN config with DefaultVlan, OuterVlanTag, InnerVlanTag.
  - VlanId, Ethertype (0x8100 for InnerVlan, 0x88a8/0x9100 for OuterVlan).
  - VlanPriorityTag, VlanCfi.
- MulticastVlanForwarding (optional).
- DstIpVlanMapping (optional): Map destination IPs to VLAN configs.
chunks.summary: EthernetTopology: per-ECU SrcIpList, SrcMacAdr, VLAN configuration; EthProtoPrioConfig sets VLAN priority per protocol.

chunks.title: Section 4: ChannelsConfig – FaultyChannels
chunks.content:
ChannelsConfig is an optional section used to define IO channels for fault injection (e.g., short circuit in a CAN bus, open wire in a LIN bus).

**FaultyChannels**: A dict of {faultType: ioHWChannel} pairs.

Example:
```yaml
ChannelsConfig:
  Io_Channel_Ex1:
    FaultyChannels: {keyFaultyType, valueIoHwChannel}
  Io_Channel_Ex2:
    FaultyChannels: {keyFaultyType, valueIoHwChannel}
```
chunks.summary: ChannelsConfig (optional): FaultyChannels maps fault types to IO hardware channels for fault injection (short circuit, open wire).

chunks.title: Complete MTF Configuration File Example (CM + BTS + PCAP + Tracers)
chunks.content:
Complete example for a setup with CM, BTS-EVO, and PCAP adapter:

```yaml
Channels:
 Ethernet_Switch:
   Id: 8
   Type: ETHERNET
   TracerName: PCAP_Tracer_ETH
 CAN_FD_ch1:
   Id: 9
   TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_CAN
   Type: CANFD
   Protocol: CANFD
 CAN_ch1:
   Id: 11
   TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_CAN
   Type: CAN
   Protocol: CAN2.0
 FlexRay_ch1:
   Id: 13
   TracerName: ASCII_Tracer_FLEXRAY
   LoggingName: A_FlexRay
   Type: FR

Mappings:
  CM:
    Devices:
      1:
        Id: 64
        Type: CAN_Combo
        Buses:
          CAN_ch1:
            HWChannel: 10
          FlexRay_ch1:
            HWChannel: 12
            OperationMode: Normal
            KeySlot: 64
            NodeType: ColdStartLeading
            WakeUpCluster: false
  BTS:
    Boards:
      1:
        Id: 8
        Type: BaseBoard
        Version: EVO
        Buses:
          CAN_FD_ch1:
            OperationMode: Normal
            HWChannel: 2
  PCAP:
    1:
      Adapter:
        Name: Ethernet_Switch
        FriendlyName: "Ethernet_Switch"
        BufferSize: 1024
        PacketProcessingActive: true
        PacketIdentificationActive: true
        DataLoggerType: TECMP

FrameworkConfig:
  Tracing:
    PCAP_Tracer_ETH:
      Type: PCAP
      LoggingType: StandardMode
      LoggerConfiguration:
        FileConfig:
          BaseFileName: ETH_BTS_CM
          Extension: .pcap
    ASCII_Tracer_CAN:
      Type: ASCII
      Base: Decimal
      TimeStamp: Microsecond
      TimeStampSetting: Absolute
      InternalEventLogged: true
      LoggerConfiguration:
        FileConfig:
          BaseFileName: can
          Extension: .asc
```
chunks.summary: Complete MTF configuration example covering Channels (CAN, CANFD, FlexRay, Ethernet) with CM, BTS, PCAP mappings and ASCII/PCAP tracers.

chunks.title: Complete Example – Power Supply + BTS-Revo Configuration
chunks.content:
Example for a setup with a Genesys power supply and BTS-Revo board:

```yaml
Channels:
  PS_bts_Ch:
    Id: 70
    TracerName: default_ascii_tracer
    LoggingName: PowerSupply
    Type: PS
  Ch1-BTS:
    Id: 72
    TracerName: default_ascii_tracer
    Type: IOOUTPUT
  Ch3-BTS:
    Id: 73
    TracerName: default_ascii_tracer
    Type: IOOUTPUT

Mappings:
  Genesys_PowerSupply:
    Channels:
      1:
        BitRate: 9600
        ChannelName: PS_bts_Ch
        DefaultMaxCurrent: 120
        DefaultVoltage: 12
        MaxVoltage: 20
        PortName: COM9
        KeepStatus: true
  BTS-Revo:
    Boards:
      1:
        Id: 160
        IOs:
          Ch1-BTS:
            HWChannel: 1
            MeasurementAttribute: Voltage
          Ch3-BTS:
            HWChannel: 3
            Function: VBATSwitch
            MeasurementAttribute: Voltage
```
chunks.summary: Full example with PS-type logical channels, Genesys power supply mapping, and BTS-Revo IO mapping with VBATSwitch function.
